penalty: Execution by the sword; strictly no ransom; dragged even from God's altar.
rationale: Grounded in Imago Dei—human life bears God's image and cannot be monetised. Unpunished murder defiles the land.

penalty: Exile to one of six Levitical Cities of Refuge (Arei Miklat) until the High Priest's death; no ransom.
rationale: Shields the unintentional killer from the avenger of blood (Go'el HaDam), halting blood feuds whilst honouring the gravity of life lost.

offence: Unsolved Homicide on the Open Road
penalty: Elders break a heifer's neck in a rough, unploughed valley by a stream; valley never sown.
rationale: Expiates communal bloodguilt when the perpetrator remains undiscovered.

offence: Owner Negligence with a Known Dangerous Ox
penalty: Ox stoned (flesh uneaten); negligent owner faces death or court-imposed ransom.
rationale: Holds property owners criminally accountable when warned of a lethal hazard.

offence: Theft of an Ox (Slaughtered or Sold)
penalty: Fivefold restitution (five oxen for one stolen ox).
rationale: Higher multiplier reflects both premeditated disposal of evidence and the ox's crucial agricultural labour value.

offence: Theft of a Sheep (Slaughtered or Sold)
penalty: Fourfold restitution (four sheep for one stolen sheep).
rationale: Deters livestock rustling whilst keeping property offences non-capital.

penalty: Double restitution (200%); if unable to pay, temporary bonded servitude until debt is cleared.
rationale: Restores the victim twofold without resorting to execution for property crimes.

penalty: Full restitution from the best of the offender's field/vineyard, or full fire damages.
rationale: Enforces civil stewardship and strict accountability for agricultural negligence.

penalty: Monetary compensation for lost wages/time and full medical care until healed.
rationale: Translates proportional justice into practical economic restoration.

penalty: Proportional court-assessed damages (or husband's court-approved fine if mother unharmed in premature birth).
rationale: Establishes an equitable ceiling on retaliation—interpreted in judicial practice as financial compensation rather than personal vendetta.

offence: Master Maiming a Servant's Eye or Tooth
penalty: Immediate, unconditional emancipation (freedom) of the servant.
rationale: Protects the bodily dignity of servants and checks abusive authority.

penalty: Infliction of stripes strictly capped at 40 (39 in practice).
rationale: Prevents judicial cruelty so an offender is not degraded in the sight of the community.

penalty: Death by execution whether sold or held in possession.
rationale: Treats theft of human liberty as an unpardonable capital crime rather than a mere economic tort.

penalty: Death by execution (or stoning for the persistently rebellious son).
rationale: Safeguards the fifth commandment and the foundational authority of the family unit.

penalty: Minimum two eyewitnesses required; false witnesses suffer the exact penalty they plotted against the accused.
rationale: Prevents hasty verdicts and deters malicious abuse of capital courts.

penalty: No punishment; full exoneration of the coerced victim.
rationale: Distinguishes moral culpability from forced compliance when no aid was available.

offence: Hidden Sacral Breaches (Blood, Chametz, Circumcision, Impurity)
penalty: Karet ('cut off from one's people'): punitive expulsion or divine premature death / spiritual excision.
rationale: Governs private or sacral covenant violations beyond eyewitness court jurisdiction.

offence: Public Sabbath Defiance, Blasphemy, or Molech Worship
penalty: Judicial stoning (Sekilah) by the community; divine Karet if human justice fails.
rationale: Dual sanction protects both public covenant loyalty and communal holiness.

penalty: Pay 50-shekel bride price (mohar) and marry her (or pay mohar if father refuses).
rationale: Secures the woman's economic and social standing.

offence: Deceitful Weights & Harm to Resident Aliens
penalty: Equal statutory restitution and prohibition on inaccurate weights; identical law for alien and native.
rationale: Eliminates commercial fraud and enforces impartial justice regardless of birth status.

penalty: No bloodguilt if a thief breaking in at night is struck dead; bloodguilt if the sun had already risen.
rationale: At night the householder cannot judge the intruder's intent or identity; in daylight the intruder can be seen, stopped or caught, so killing him is bloodshed.

offence: Avenger vs. the Manslayer in Refuge
penalty: The avenger who kills a manslayer found outside the refuge city before the High Priest's death has no bloodguilt; inside the city, or after the High Priest's death, he is a murderer.
rationale: The city of refuge is a real boundary: it protects the manslayer inside it and limits the avenger's right outside it.

penalty: Thief caught: pays double. Thief not found: the keeper swears before the judges. Rival claims: the party the judges condemn pays double.
rationale: Places the burden on the guilty party and uses an oath before God and the judges where proof is missing, not automatic liability for the keeper.

penalty: Borrower pays if the animal dies while the owner is away; no payment if the owner was present or the animal was hired; keeper pays for theft but not if a beast tore it and he brings the remains.
rationale: Liability follows control and risk: the one who had the animal and benefited bears the loss, unless the owner was there or the loss was beyond the keeper's control.

penalty: Return a neighbour's strayed ox or donkey; if the owner is far or unknown, keep it until he seeks it; help lift a fallen animal even if it belongs to an enemy.
rationale: Neighbourly duty applies even to rivals; finders do not acquire what they find.

offence: Ox Kills a Servant or Another Ox
penalty: Servant killed: 30 shekels to the master and the ox is stoned. Ox kills ox: sell the living ox and divide the price (unwarned owner) or pay ox for ox (warned owner).
rationale: Compensation scales with warning and the victim's status, and the ox's owner is liable only if he knew the beast was dangerous.

penalty: Whoever kills an animal makes it good: life for life, a living animal of equal value.
rationale: Lex talionis here means exact replacement, not a human life for an animal's.

penalty: No bribes; no siding with the poor out of pity or with the great out of awe; judge your neighbour fairly.
rationale: A bribe blinds the wise; partiality in either direction perverts justice.

penalty: Pay a poor labourer his wage the same day, before sunset; never hold it overnight, whether he is a countryman or a resident alien.
rationale: A poor labourer's wage is his food for the day; withholding it is oppression.

penalty: No interest on loans to a poor Israelite or resident alien; interest may be charged to a foreigner (nokhri) passing through for trade.
rationale: Loans to the needy are an act of covenant kindness, not a market; commercial loans to foreign traders are treated differently.

penalty: A cloak taken in pledge goes back before sunset; no millstone or widow's garment as a pledge; the creditor waits outside while the debtor brings the pledge out.
rationale: A pledge may never strip the debtor of his livelihood, his night's warmth or the dignity of his home.

penalty: Goes free in the seventh year without payment, with the wife he brought; a wife given by the master and her children stay with the master; a servant who loves his master may have his ear pierced and serve permanently.
rationale: A time limit on servitude, in contrast to ANE chattel slavery, with a voluntary route to permanent service.

penalty: Do not return a runaway servant to his master; let him dwell where he chooses and do not oppress him.
rationale: Directly reverses ANE codes that punished anyone sheltering a runaway.

penalty: Sons inherit; daughters if there are no sons; then brothers. The firstborn takes a double portion even if his mother is the unloved wife.
rationale: Inheritance follows the law, not the father's favouritism.

penalty: Those unclean through a corpse or on a distant journey keep the Passover a month later; one who is clean and at home but neglects it is cut off.
rationale: Mercy for genuine inability; Karet for deliberate neglect.

penalty: Unwitting sin: a year-old female goat as a sin offering. High-handed sin: the offender is cut off (Karet).
rationale: Intent decides between atonement by offering and excision.
